newsitem.title: USA: Corp bond players anxiously await Raytheon launch.
newsitem.headline: Corp bond players anxiously await Raytheon launch.

text.p: Before the launch of defense contractor Raytheon Co's $2.5 billion debt offering, underwriters may have to boost the size of the deal to meet growing demand, corporate bond players said.

"All three tranches right now are issue-bid on the street," said one high-grade syndicate source. "It's tough to figure out which issues will be upsized as they're all meeting with an equal amount of demand."
Meanwhile, the current breakdown on the multi-tranche debt offering is as follows, according to players.
-- $1.0 billion five-year debt, unofficial price talk between 40 and 45 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries,
-- $1.0 billion 10-year debt, unofficial price talk between 60 and 65 basis points over Treasuries,
-- $500 million in 30-year debt, unofficial price talk at 75 to 80 basis points over Treasuries.
The 10-year is expected to have a make-whole call provision of 10 basis points over Treasuries. The 30-year is also expected to have a make-whole at 15 basis points over the curve, sources said.
Morgan Stanley Dean Witter is lead manager for the deal.
Players said Raytheon has only taken down $2.5 billion of its $3.0 billion shelf registration filed on May 23, leaving room for the deal to be expanded.
"The deal is obviously in great shape, so there's no caution here," said another syndicate source.

"The upcoming (Treasury) auctions of 10's and 30's are going to play a role in where the market is going, but I don't think accounts are waiting to buy until after they're done; Raytheon's deal is already issue-bid -- the demand is there," he said.
Seperately, players have been closely monitoring the new bulk of Treasury supply coming in, hoping good auctions will bolster weaker Treasury prices and send yields to more attractive levels.
Treasuries fell sharply last week on bullish U.S. employment and manufacturing data, sparking a sharp rise in interest rates and pushing corporate bond issuers to the sidelines.
Meanwhile, players will be watching Wednesday's sale of $12 billion 10-year notes by Treasury followed by Thursday's $10 billion in 30-year supply.
Currently, the benchmark 30-year bond is up 2/32 at 101-26/32 to yield 6.49 percent. Just a week ago, the T-bond was yielding 6.32 percent at the close.

Despite the upturn in long-term interest rates names continue to appear in the corporate bond market. However, most are expected to ride out the bulk of corporate and government supply this week, dealers said.
Among names currently in the market are Meditrust Healthcare's $400 million debt offering, Staples Inc's $200 million deal and Summit Properties' $100 million issue, dealer said.
In the high-yield arena, a slew of new junk issues are slated to hit the market this week, players said.

ICN Pharmaceuticals Inc is expected to issue a $200 million debt offering, MRS Logistica SA is expected to sell $320 million in a Euro/144a offering and another $200 million in 10-year debt is expected to come from Signature Resorts Inc , sources said. is seen between 10-10.25 percent.

B&G Foods will sell $100 million in 10-year 144a notes, Golden Ocean Group will set $150 million in seven-year 144a notes, Insilco Corp will sell $150 milllion and Atlas Air is slated to bring $100 million in eight-year debt, sources said.
